full_judgment:
Inspite of the presumption of truth attached to oral evidence under oath if the Court is not satisfied, the evidence inspite of oath is of no avail. 

 Cognizance to which the accused is called upon to plead is a very important document. It should be drawn up and considered with extreme care and caution, so that accused may have no doubt whatever as to the offences to which he is called upon to answer and the Judge of the Appellate Court also may have no doubt upon the matter. The word 'Ground' means basis, foundation or valid reason. The whole object of taking cognizance is to enable the defence to concentrate its attention on the case that he has to meet. Conditions for taking cognizance are (i) presumption of the commission of an offence on the materials before the Court and (ii) offences triable exclusively by a competent Court.
